newsitem.title: UK: Police arrive to break up North Sea port blockade.
newsitem.headline: Police arrive to break up North Sea port blockade.

text.p: Local police have reached the fishing boats blockading the Sullom Voe oil terminal on the Shetland Islands and are ordering protesters to leave the harbour, an official said.

"Police arrived at 1130 (1030 GMT) and have already been round about half the vessels telling them the special directive is in force," said Malcolm Green, chief executive of the Shetland Islands council.
The Shetland Islands council issued the special directive late on Monday ordering the fourteen boats to leave the port area by 0300 (0200 GMT) on Tuesday.
Green said the fishermen would be given a short time to follow police orders and leave the port, after which they would be charged with a criminal offence.
Earlier, one of the protesters told Reuters that the boats would not move until the fishermen had received legal documents from the police.
The crews could also face civil penalties which may include the substantial costs of delaying huge ocean going oil tankers, local officials said.
The fishermen are protesting against unpaid compensation claims from the International Oil Pollution Compensation Fund (IOPCF) for damage caused to fishing grounds by the Braer tanker spill in 1993.
The Sullom Voe terminal handles one fifth of Britain's oil output and is the export terminal for world benchmark crude Brent blend.
The blockade prevented a fully-loaded tanker from leaving the port on schedule at 0700 (0600 GMT) on Tuesday.
